The setup cost is **136.4441474007699** per production run, and the startup cost is **72.08169936581939** per startup. The holding cost for Item 0 is **1.045681545748948** per unit, for Item 1 is **1.076278851472706** per unit, and for Item 2 is **1.141130030903227** per unit. The backlogging cost for Item 0 is **7.516688931886524** per unit, for Item 1 is **6.810219227144024** per unit, and for Item 2 is **7.989326755092092** per unit.

The production system involves three items (Item 0, Item 1, and Item 2), two machines (Machine 0 and Machine 1), and three time periods (Period 0, Period 1, and Period 2). For each item, machine, and time period, decide whether to produce the item (binary decision) and how much to produce (continuous decision). Determine whether to start up a machine for a specific item in a given period (binary decision). Decide how much inventory to carry over or how much demand to backlog for each item in each period (continuous decisions).

The total production, inventory, and backlog must balance the demand for each item in each period. For example, in Period 0, the demand for Item 0 is **15.13481645049243**, for Item 1 is **15.96509719647714**, and for Item 2 is **15.05799468831989**. In Period 1, the demand for Item 0 is **23.22348134905647**, for Item 1 is **24.89682877145792**, and for Item 2 is **20.28924491987942**. In Period 2, the demand for Item 0 is **19.81696900208589**, for Item 1 is **22.4702270586731**, and for Item 2 is **18.30123580755789**.

The production quantity and startup time must not exceed the machine's capacity. Machine 0 has a capacity of **74.37564803880434**, and starting it up requires **6.598818345230923** units of time. Machine 1 has a capacity of **61.80119129480688**, and starting it up requires **6.132700881798776** units of time. Each machine can produce only one item at a time in any given period. For example, in Period 0, Machine 0 can produce either Item 0, Item 1, or Item 2, but not more than one. Similarly, Machine 1 can produce only one item at a time in any period.

If a machine is used to produce an item in a period after being idle in the previous period, a startup cost is incurred. For example, if Machine 0 is used to produce Item 0 in Period 1 but was not used in Period 0, a startup cost of **72.08169936581939** is incurred. Production quantities, inventory levels, and backlogs must be non-negative. Production and startup decisions are binary (either 0 or 1).

The goal is to determine the optimal production, startup, inventory, and backlog decisions for each item, machine, and time period to minimize the total cost while satisfying all constraints.

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    items = d["items"]
    machines = d["machines"]
    periods = d["periods"]

    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=items)
    model.M = pyo.Set(initialize=machines)
    model.T = pyo.Set(initialize=periods)

    # Production quantity
    model.produce = pyo.Var(model.I, model.M, model.T,
                            within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    # Whether item i is produced on machine m in period t
    model.setup = pyo.Var(model.I, model.M, model.T,
                          within=pyo.Binary)
    # Whether machine m starts up for item i in period t
    model.startup = pyo.Var(model.I, model.M, model.T,
                            within=pyo.Binary)
    # Inventory carried for item i at end of period t
    model.inventory = pyo.Var(model.I, model.T,
                              within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    # Backlog for item i at end of period t
    model.backlog = pyo.Var(model.I, model.T,
                            within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Objective: setup + startup + holding + backlog costs
    def obj_rule(m):
        setup_term = d["setup_cost"] * sum(
            m.setup[i, mm, t] for i in m.I for mm in m.M for t in m.T)
        startup_term = d["startup_cost"] * sum(
            m.startup[i, mm, t] for i in m.I for mm in m.M for t in m.T)
        holding_term = sum(
            d["holding_cost"][i] * m.inventory[i, t]
            for i in m.I for t in m.T)
        backlog_term = sum(
            d["backlog_cost"][i] * m.backlog[i, t]
            for i in m.I for t in m.T)
        return setup_term + startup_term + holding_term + backlog_term

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Inventory / backlog balance for each item and period
    def balance_rule(m, i, t):
        production = sum(m.produce[i, mm, t] for mm in m.M)
        prev_inv = m.inventory[i, t - 1] if t > 0 else 0.0
        prev_back = m.backlog[i, t - 1] if t > 0 else 0.0
        return (prev_inv + production + m.backlog[i, t]
                - m.inventory[i, t] - prev_back == d["demand"][(i, t)])

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.T, rule=balance_rule)

    # Production cannot exceed machine capacity when setup is on
    def prod_capacity_rule(m, i, mm, t):
        return m.produce[i, mm, t] <= d["machine_capacity"][mm] * m.setup[i, mm, t]

    model.prod_capacity = pyo.Constraint(
        model.I, model.M, model.T, rule=prod_capacity_rule)

    # Total machine time (production + startup) cannot exceed capacity
    def machine_time_rule(m, mm, t):
        production_time = sum(m.produce[i, mm, t] for i in m.I)
        startup_usage = d["startup_time"][mm] * sum(
            m.startup[i, mm, t] for i in m.I)
        return production_time + startup_usage <= d["machine_capacity"][mm]

    model.machine_time = pyo.Constraint(
        model.M, model.T, rule=machine_time_rule)

    # At most one item per machine per period
    def one_item_rule(m, mm, t):
        return sum(m.setup[i, mm, t] for i in m.I) <= 1

    model.one_item = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=one_item_rule)

    # Startup linking: startup occurs when machine goes from idle to active
    def startup_rule(m, i, mm, t):
        prev_setup = m.setup[i, mm, t - 1] if t > 0 else 0.0
        return m.startup[i, mm, t] >= m.setup[i, mm, t] - prev_setup

    model.startup_link = pyo.Constraint(
        model.I, model.M, model.T, rule=startup_rule)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):

    items = d["items"]
    machines = d["machines"]
    periods = d["periods"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=items)
    model.Mc = pyo.Set(initialize=machines)   # avoid Block name "M" style collisions
    model.T = pyo.Set(initialize=periods)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Variables
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    model.x = pyo.Var(
        model.I, model.Mc, model.T,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
    )

    model.y = pyo.Var(
        model.I, model.Mc, model.T,
        domain=pyo.Binary,
    )

    model.st = pyo.Var(
        model.I, model.Mc, model.T,
        domain=pyo.Binary,
    )

    model.inv = pyo.Var(
        model.I, model.T,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
    )

    model.bl = pyo.Var(
        model.I, model.T,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
    )

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Objective
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    def obj_rule(m):
        expr = 0.0
        for i in m.I:
            for mm in m.Mc:
                for t in m.T:
                    expr += d["setup_cost"][i] * m.y[i, mm, t]
                    expr += d["startup_cost"] * m.st[i, mm, t]
            for t in m.T:
                expr += d["holding_cost"][i] * m.inv[i, t]
                expr += d["backlog_cost"][i] * m.bl[i, t]
        return expr

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Constraints
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------

    # 1) production linked to production-run binary
    def prod_link_rule(m, i, mm, t):
        return m.x[i, mm, t] <= d["capacity"][mm] * m.y[i, mm, t]

    model.prod_link = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.Mc, model.T, rule=prod_link_rule)

    # 2) machine capacity: production quantity + startup time <= capacity
    def capacity_rule(m, mm, t):
        usage = 0.0
        for i in m.I:
            usage += m.x[i, mm, t]
        startups = 0.0
        for i in m.I:
            startups += 1.0 * m.st[i, mm, t]
        return usage + d["startup_time"][mm] * startups <= d["capacity"][mm]

    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.Mc, model.T, rule=capacity_rule)

    # 3) each machine produces at most one item per period
    def one_item_rule(m, mm, t):
        total = 0.0
        for i in m.I:
            total += 1.0 * m.y[i, mm, t]
        return total <= 1

    model.one_item = pyo.Constraint(model.Mc, model.T, rule=one_item_rule)

    # 4) startup indicator: st >= y[t] - y[t-1]  (t >= 1)
    def startup_link_rule(m, i, mm, t):
        if t == 0:
            return m.st[i, mm, t] >= m.y[i, mm, t]
        return m.st[i, mm, t] >= m.y[i, mm, t] - m.y[i, mm, t - 1]

    model.startup_link = pyo.Constraint(
        model.I, model.Mc, model.T, rule=startup_link_rule
    )

    # 5) inventory / backlog balance for each item and period
    # inventory_{t} - backlog_{t} + backlog_{t-1} - inventory_{t-1}
    #   = production_t - demand_t
    def balance_rule(m, i, t):
        prod = 0.0
        for mm in m.Mc:
            prod += m.x[i, mm, t]
        lhs = m.inv[i, t] - m.bl[i, t]
        if t == 0:
            return lhs + prod == d["demand"][i][t]
        return (
            lhs - m.inv[i, t - 1] + m.bl[i, t - 1] + prod
            == d["demand"][i][t]
        )

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.T, rule=balance_rule)

    return model

# =============================================================================
# DECISION VARIABLES
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# x[i, m, t]  >= 0  : production quantity of item i on machine m in period t
# y[i, m, t]  binary: 1 if item i is produced on machine m in period t
# s[i, m, t]  binary: 1 if machine m starts up for item i in period t
# I[i, t]     >= 0  : inventory of item i carried from period t to t+1
# B[i, t]     >= 0  : backlog of item i at end of period t
#
# OBJECTIVE (minimize):
#   sum over (i,m,t) of [ setup_cost * y[i,m,t] + startup_cost * s[i,m,t] ]
#   + sum over (i,t) of [ holding_cost[i] * I[i,t] + backlog_cost[i] * B[i,t] ]
#
# CONSTRAINTS
# (1) Inventory balance for each item i and period t:
#       I[i,t-1] - B[i,t-1] + sum_m x[i,m,t] - I[i,t] + B[i,t] = demand[i,t]
#     (I[i,-1] = B[i,-1] = 0)
# (2) Machine capacity: production + startup time <= capacity, for each m,t:
#       sum_i x[i,m,t] + startup_time[m] * sum_i s[i,m,t] <= capacity[m]
# (3) One item per machine per period:
#       sum_i y[i,m,t] <= 1
# (4) Production only if setup binary is on (big-M):
#       x[i,m,t] <= capacity[m] * y[i,m,t]
# (5) Startup logic: s[i,m,t] >= y[i,m,t] - y[i,m,t-1]
#     (y[i,m,-1] = 0)
# =============================================================================

    def startup_rule(m, i, mm, t):

        return m.s[i, mm, t] >= m.y[i, mm, t] - prev

    model.startup = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.M, model.T, rule=startup_rule)

            d["hold_cost"][i] * m.I[i, t]
            for i in m.ITEMS for t in m.PERIODS
        )
        backlog = sum(
            d["back_cost"][i] * m.B[i, t]
            for i in m.ITEMS for t in m.PERIODS
        )
        return setup + startup + holding + backlog

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ---- (1) Inventory balance ----
    def balance_rule(m, i, t):
        prev_I = m.I[i, t - 1] if (t - 1) in PERIODS else 0.0
        prev_B = m.B[i, t - 1] if (t - 1) in PERIODS else 0.0
        production = sum(m.x[i, j, t] for j in m.MACHINES)
        return prev_I - prev_B + production - m.I[i, t] + m.B[i, t] == d["demand"][i][t]

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(
        model.ITEMS, model.PERIODS, rule=balance_rule
    )

    # ---- (2) Machine capacity ----
    def capacity_rule(m, j, t):
        production = sum(m.x[i, j, t] for i in m.ITEMS)
        startup = sum(d["startup_time"][j] * m.s[i, j, t] for i in m.ITEMS)
        return production + startup <= d["machine_cap"][j]

    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(
        model.MACHINES, model.PERIODS, rule=capacity_rule
    )

    # ---- (3) One item per machine per period ----
    def one_item_rule(m, j, t):
        return sum(m.y[i, j, t] for i in m.ITEMS) <= 1

    model.one_item = pyo.Constraint(
        model.MACHINES, model.PERIODS, rule=one_item_rule
    )

    # ---- (4) Production linked to setup indicator ----
    def link_rule(m, i, j, t):
        return m.x[i, j, t] <= d["big_m"] * m.y[i, j, t]

    model.link = pyo.Constraint(
        model.ITEMS, model.MACHINES, model.PERIODS, rule=link_rule
    )

    # ---- (5) Startup logic ----
    def startup_rule(m, i, j, t):
        prev_y = m.y[i, j, t - 1] if (t - 1) in PERIODS else 0.0
        return m.s[i, j, t] >= m.y[i, j, t] - prev_y

    model.startup = pyo.Constraint(
        model.ITEMS, model.MACHINES, model.PERIODS, rule=startup_rule
    )

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    items = d["items"]
    machines = d["machines"]
    periods = d["periods"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=items)
    model.M = pyo.Set(initialize=machines)
    model.T = pyo.Set(initialize=periods)

    # Decision variables
    model.production = pyo.Var(
        model.I, model.M, model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals
    )
    model.produce_flag = pyo.Var(
        model.I, model.M, model.T, within=pyo.Binary
    )
    model.startup = pyo.Var(
        model.I, model.M, model.T, within=pyo.Binary
    )
    model.inventory = pyo.Var(
        model.I, model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals
    )
    model.backlog = pyo.Var(
        model.I, model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals
    )

    # Objective: minimize setup + startup + holding + backlog
    def obj_rule(m):
        setup = d["setup_cost"] * sum(
            m.produce_flag[i, mm, t] for i in m.I for mm in m.M for t in m.T
        )
        startup = d["startup_cost"] * sum(
            m.startup[i, mm, t] for i in m.I for mm in m.M for t in m.T
        )
        holding = sum(
            d["holding_cost"][i] * m.inventory[i, t]
            for i in m.I for t in m.T
        )
        backlog = sum(
            d["backlog_cost"][i] * m.backlog[i, t]
            for i in m.I for t in m.T
        )
        return setup + startup + holding + backlog

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Inventory balance per item and period
    def balance_rule(m, i, t):
        prev_inv = m.inventory[i, t - 1] if t > 0 else 0.0
        prev_back = m.backlog[i, t - 1] if t > 0 else 0.0
        total_prod = sum(m.production[i, mm, t] for mm in m.M)
        return (
            prev_inv
            - prev_back
            + total_prod
            - m.inventory[i, t]
            + m.backlog[i, t]
            == d["demand"][(i, t)]
        )

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.T, rule=balance_rule)

    # Machine capacity: production + startup time <= capacity
    def capacity_rule(m, mm, t):
        prod_time = sum(m.production[i, mm, t] for i in m.I)
        startup_time = d["startup_time"][mm] * sum(
            m.startup[i, mm, t] for i in m.I
        )
        return prod_time + startup_time <= d["machine_capacity"][mm]

    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=capacity_rule)

    # At most one item per machine per period
    def one_item_rule(m, mm, t):
        return sum(m.produce_flag[i, mm, t] for i in m.I) <= 1

    model.one_item = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=one_item_rule)

    # Production <= big-M * produce_flag (link production to flag)
    big_m = max(d["machine_capacity"].values())

    def link_rule(m, i, mm, t):
        return m.production[i, mm, t] <= big_m * m.produce_flag[i, mm, t]

    model.link = pyo.Constraint(model.I, model.M, model.T, rule=link_rule)

    # Startup logic: startup >= produce_flag(t) - produce_flag(t-1)
    def startup_rule(m, i, mm, t):
        prev = m.produce_flag[i, mm, t - 1] if t > 0 else 0
        return m.startup[i, mm, t] >= m.produce_flag[i, mm, t] - prev

    model.startup_logic = pyo.Constraint(
        model.I, model.M, model.T, rule=startup_rule
    )

    # Startup only when producing
    def startup_link_rule(m, i, mm, t):
        return m.startup[i, mm, t] <= m.produce_flag[i, mm, t]

    model.startup_link = pyo.Constraint(
        model.I, model.M, model.T, rule=startup_link_rule
    )

    return model
